## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the fused integrate-decide loop with a mask-based respawn scan can approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The 69 B/p AoS layout (68 struct + 1 mask byte) offers poor locality: loop 1 touches 28/68 B/p (41% hot), loop 2 touches 4/68 (5%), loop 3 touches 28/68 (41%). The 1 B/p mask is loop 1's sole output and loop 2's sole input. The approach fuses math+decide into an auto-vectorizable loop 1, then host-scans the mask in loop 2. With 59-95% dead bytes per line, most bandwidth is wasted; the working set spills L1d at N≈474 and L2 at N≈7598, so most points run from L2 or deeper.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p rises from 21.6 (L1d, N=320) to ~24.5 (L3, N=10000) to 26.7 (DRAM, N=10000000). No knee at L1d→L2 (N≈474): flat at 21.7-22.0 from N=480-1200. L2→L3 at N≈7598 adds ~1 ns/p. L3→DRAM at N≈243K is mild at q=0.01 but sharpens with death rate: q=0.25 jumps from 28.0 (N=160000) to 32.7 (N=370000). Transitions are shallow — the algo runs 4x above the 5.437 ns/p floor, so cache latency barely perturbs a compute/branch-bound kernel.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.0-3.2 GB/s against 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 16-25%. The 5.437 ns/p floor frames irreducible memory time; this algo runs 21-34 ns/p, 4-6x above — compute/branch-bound.
